clue.text: Power with which great performer's gained speed

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
an ace is a star performer, the best at something

explanation.surface: A star performer has gained speed through sheer power.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace is a rate of movement, a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Model that may get someone easily caught out

definitions.meaning: someone who sits for an artist or photographer

definitions.text: that may get someone easily caught out
definitions.meaning: in cricket, an easy catch that the fielder should never drop

explanation.surface: A model whose pose might trap someone into an easy mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'caught out' when a fielder catches the ball; a gentle, simple chance is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model sits for portraits; a dolly catch in cricket goes by the same word.

clue.text: Rosemary maybe wants some other boy

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rosemary, a woman, fancies a different boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'wants' into the definition, but no plant-word means 'rosemary maybe wants'; 'wants' is a link joining definition to wordplay. Rosemary reads as a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic kitchen plant, an example of the culinary class, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Meeting the Spanish, Greek characters cheat

indicators.note: meeting puts the two pieces next to each other, the Greek letters joined by the Spanish article

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, here in the plural
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Greek players meeting Spanish ones are accused of cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: To chisel is informal for swindling or defrauding someone.

clue.text: An attachment to what money will buy

definitions.text: An attachment to what money will buy

parts.words: An attachment to what money will buy
parts.note: a little label fixed to goods in a shop, showing their cost; 'attachment' suggests affection for wealth

explanation.surface: Someone's fondness for things that can be bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop goods carry a small label tied or stuck on to show their cost.

clue.text: Order money to be paid to agent

definitions.meaning: to place an order for a piece of work, as with a portrait

definitions.text: money to be paid to agent
definitions.meaning: the percentage fee a salesperson or broker earns on a deal

explanation.surface: An instruction that cash be handed to a representative.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both requesting a piece of work and an agent's percentage fee.

clue.text: Singer in pub, one having vocal expression

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place
I is the Roman numeral one
tone of voice is the way something is said

explanation.surface: A singer in a pub, someone with an expressive voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass, so a kind of singer.

clue.text: See tragic king die horribly in classical work

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the word for a musical work

parts.note: an opus is a numbered musical composition

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters of die are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Go and watch a tragic king die gruesomely in a classical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link, as in 'go and see'; 'classical work' tempts towards a Greek play, but it is a musical one. 'horribly' makes EDI, and 'in' sets it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theban ruler of Sophocles' drama, who unknowingly killed his father and wed his mother.

clue.text: Essex town not totally tough and mean!

indicators.note: not totally says the word for tough loses its final letter

parts.note: hard means tough
low means mean or base

explanation.surface: A jibe at an Essex town as rough and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' trims HARD to HAR. Essex is a county just north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A new town in Essex, England, built after the Second World War.

clue.text: Man by the briny in a deck chair, say?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the briny is a jocular name for the sea
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man lounges by the sea in a deck chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a deck chair is sitting down, an example hence 'say?'.

clue.text: Improper posturing where mountaineers gather

parts.note: base means low or morally improper
camp means affected or theatrical posing

explanation.surface: Inappropriate showing off at a climbers' meeting point.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers assemble at the main camp low on a mountain before the ascent.

clue.text: There is apparel specially designed for artists

indicators.note: specially designed suggests the clothing is made over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothing has been tailor-made for some artists.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian brotherhood of English painters including Rossetti and Millais.

clue.text: Member of family carries nothing around? Big van can do that job

definitions.text: Big van can do that job

indicators.note: carries says the family member holds the other letters within

parts.note: a relation is a family member
O looks like zero, nothing
C is short for circa, around

explanation.surface: A relative ferries nothing about, though a big van could manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for circa, Latin for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A removal van carries out a house move, which is the job described.

clue.text: A deceiver's no right to get assumed 24

indicators.note: no right means the abbreviation for right is dropped

parts.note: a liar is a deceiver; with the 's it gives an S

explanation.surface: A liar has no right to adopt a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 refers to the answer at 24-down, so the definition reads 'assumed name'.
explanation.definitionFit: A false identity someone takes on is a pseudonym, an assumed moniker.

clue.text: To move house is appropriate when lake encroaches

indicators.note: encroaches says the lake letter intrudes into the other word

parts.note: fit means suitable or appropriate
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Relocating is advisable when the lake starts creeping closer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British and Scottish usage, to change residence, often quietly or by night.

clue.text: Outside entrance to minster more than one choirboy shakes

indicators.note: outside says the boys' word goes around the initial letter

parts.note: trebles are boy sopranos in a choir

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Several choirboys tremble outside the door of the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver or shiver is to shake.

clue.text: Move sack

definitions.meaning: a sack dress, a loose straight dress

explanation.surface: Instruction to relocate a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like dismissal or a bag, but it is a sack dress, a simple loose garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to relocate; the noun is a loose straight dress also called a sack.

clue.text: Session of instruction a prominent feature after meal

indicators.note: after places the facial feature behind the meal

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal
a chin is a feature of the face that sticks out

explanation.surface: A lesson with a noticeable element following food.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal lecture and discussion meeting on a topic, a session of instruction.

clue.text: Frame awkwardly rigid I removed

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of rigid are jumbled
removed says the letter I is taken from the jumble

explanation.surface: A frame that is clumsily stiff, with one part taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take an I from RIGID, leaving R, G, I, D, and rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice or network of bars is a framework.

clue.text: Firm's reputation? Distinct danger that will be ruined

indicators.note: ruined says the phrase is wrecked and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A company's good name faces a clear threat of ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's financial trustworthiness in the eyes of lenders.

clue.text: Evening worker

parts.note: evening reads as night-time but means smoothing out creases in laundry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' suggests a night shift, but here it is the verb 'evening', making flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presses laundry smooths it flat, making garments even.

clue.text: Rejection of agreement restricting one part of UK

indicators.note: restricting says the agreement holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a deal is an agreement
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Turning down a pact that limits a region of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing or rejecting a claim or request is a refusal.

clue.text: Short piece delivered to the world is uncompromising

parts.note: a stub is a short leftover piece
born means delivered at birth

explanation.surface: A brief item handed out to everyone is unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and refusing to yield, unwilling to compromise.

clue.text: Celebrity having an upset, this particular writer

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word is turned upside down

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A star gets upset, as does the writer of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, a celebrity.

clue.text: Virtuous husband, individual type to be given halo

parts.note: one means a single individual
ST abbreviates saint, a person shown with a halo

explanation.surface: A good husband, the sort to be called a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and truthful, of good moral character.

clue.text: One and only fish in sea area

definitions.meaning: one of the areas in the BBC Shipping Forecast, south-west of Britain

explanation.walkthrough: The Shipping Forecast is a BBC radio weather bulletin for sea areas around Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unique, names a flatfish, and labels a Shipping Forecast sea area.

clue.text: Stick together at this place having joined company

indicators.note: having joined says the two pieces are linked up side by side

parts.note: here means at this place

explanation.surface: Staying united here after joining a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To form a united whole, to hold together firmly.

clue.text: Fellows count without using pencil and paper?

parts.note: men are fellows
a tally is a count

explanation.surface: Chaps count up without writing anything down.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing sums in one's head rather than on paper is calculation by mind alone.
